title: Orange Retail Finance raises Rs 100 crore in debt, adds Rs 100 crore Shriram co-lending partnership to fuel expansion
excerpt: 13 years ago, Orange Retail Finance was a Chennai lender writing loans for two-wheelers sold through dealerships. Last month, it raised Rs 100 crore in debt from investors and added a Rs 100 crore co-lending partnership with Shriram, both aimed at funding a very different loan book. The Rs 100 crore came through listed non-convertible debentures (NCD) arranged with UMI Capital. It is half of a Rs 200 crore NCD programme the company set up for this financial year, and part of a wider Rs 300 crore debt target it plans to meet through further issuances and borrowing from banks and other institutions. Notably, Orange is also planning to raise Rs 100 crore of equity capital. The partnership with Shriram The co-lending partnership with Shriram gives Orange Rs 100 crore to lend without putting the full amount on its own balance sheet. In a co-lending arrangement , the larger partner takes most of each loan onto its books while the smaller NBFC originates the loan, keeps the customer relationship and holds a minority share. For a lender of Orange's size, it is the difference between growing at the pace its own capital allows and growing at the pace its branches can actually find customers. This is not new territory for the company. Co-lending already funds about a quarter of what Orange has out on loan, with three NBFC partners accounting for roughly Rs 101 crore of its book as of June, according to ICRA. Adding Shriram, one of India's largest retail NBFCs, extends that model considerably. Expanding beyond two-wheeler loans Orange had Rs 401 crore in assets under management as of 30 June 2026 and is targeting Rs 550 crore by the end of this financial year, which means growing roughly 37% in the remaining months. The growth is meant to come from gold loans and MSME loans against property rather than two-wheelers, with home loans and other secured products alongside them. And that shift is already visible: loans against property made up 58% of the book in June, overtaking two-wheelers at 41%. Six months earlier, the ratio was the other way round. Gold loans are the newer bet and are starting from a much smaller base. The company has said every one of its branches will have gold loan infrastructure in place by October 2026, which is what turns a product it currently does very little of into something that can carry a share of the year's target. Orange currently runs 58 branches across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, and plans to reach 150 branches and about 1,500 employees, with a longer-term ambition of Rs 3,000 crore in AUM by FY31. The company has been through a few cycles while getting here. It has traded through demonetisation in 2016 and the COVID-19 years, and said each of those forced it to rebuild rather than hold on to what it had, including its credit and risk frameworks and its move away from a dealer-led model. Onboarding CXO team To support this expansion, Orange has onboarded a CXO team across finance, business and operations, risk, technology and treasury to tighten governance, risk management and financial discipline as it scales. “We want to combine the strength of our people and customer relationships with the intelligence of technology and the discipline of institutional finance. That is how we believe we can build a financial institution that lasts,” said Ebenezer Daniel G, Founder and CEO of Orange Retail Finance. On technology, Orange is investing in AI, automation and digital credit processes , but frames it as support for staff who already know the local market rather than a replacement for them. Ebenezer Daniel said the company's 13 years had taught it that the strongest organisations are not those that simply survive difficult times but those with the courage to transform because of them. “Our ambition is not merely to become larger, but to become a trusted neighbourhood financial institution, one that stays close to customers, understands communities and creates meaningful value in their lives,” Ebenezer Daniel added.

title: Current Affairs One-Liner: 3rd October 2026
excerpt: National: On 30 September 2026 , the Union Cabinet approved an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) for Delhi with an estimated cost of ₹1,789.52 crore . The project will cover 42 major traffic corridors and use technologies such as AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, automatic enforcement and real-time traffic monitoring. It is intended to reduce congestion, improve emergency-vehicle movement and strengthen traffic management. The same Cabinet meeting also approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III , making both decisions important infrastructure-related developments. On 30 September 2026 , Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched implementation guidelines for National Coastal Mission 2.0 (NCM 2.0) in New Delhi. The ₹767-crore Central Sector Scheme will operate until 2030-31 across nine coastal states and four Union Territories . It focuses on coastal ecosystem restoration, pollution management, vulnerability assessment, sustainable tourism, biodiversity conservation and climate resilience. The programme also seeks to unlock opportunities under India’s Blue Economy while protecting coastal communities and natural ecosystems. On 2 October 2026 , the Tamil Nadu government expanded the Vettri Payanam free bus travel scheme for women and transgender persons. A total of 12,692 government buses were brought under the expanded programme, including several express, deluxe and mofussil services. The scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day . By reducing travel costs, the initiative aims to improve access to employment, education, healthcare and public services while promoting greater mobility and economic participation among women. On 2 October 2026 , the Government of India, in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh, formally identified 28 places and geographical features using standard names on the official Survey of India map . These include peaks, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes and land areas. The move is intended to improve accurate geographical identification and public awareness. Some of the locations are in strategically sensitive areas of Ladakh, making the development important from both administrative and national-security perspectives. On 2 October 2026 , Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal under the Mumbai Port Authority was declared India’s first plastic-free oil terminal . The announcement was made during Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 led by Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal . The initiative focuses on eliminating single-use plastic and making port operations more environmentally sustainable. Jawahar Dweep is an important petroleum-handling facility of Mumbai Port, and its plastic-free status supports broader cleanliness and sustainability efforts in India’s maritime sector. On 2 October 2026 , the foundation stone was laid for the Global Horticulture Hub – Rayalaseema Rising at Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh . The project envisages investment of around ₹1 lakh crore and is planned in three phases across 10 districts. It will cover 201 clusters, more than 300 mandals and thousands of villages. The project aims to strengthen horticulture production, food processing, exports, logistics and farmer incomes while positioning Rayalaseema as a major global horticulture and agri-business centre. In October 2026 , President Droupadi Murmu gave assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 , clearing the final constitutional step required before implementation by the state. The law seeks to establish a common framework for selected civil matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and related personal-law issues. Gujarat had already passed the Bill earlier in 2026, so the fresh development is specifically the President’s assent , rather than introduction of the legislation itself. Banking: On 30 September 2026 , the Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved the proposed acquisition of certain equity shares in IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company Limited by BNP Paribas Cardif . BNP Paribas Cardif is a wholly owned subsidiary of France-based BNP Paribas, while IndiaFirst Life is an IRDAI-licensed life insurer operating in India. The CCI examines mergers and acquisitions to ensure that proposed combinations do not adversely affect competition. On 30 September 2026 , Jio Financial Services Ltd and Allianz Europe B.V. jointly invested ₹640.10 crore in their 50:50 joint venture, Jio Allianz General Insurance Ltd , through a rights issue. Each partner contributed ₹320.05 crore . The funds are intended to support the insurer’s business operations and expansion. Jio Financial and Allianz had earlier entered into a 50:50 partnership covering general and health insurance, combining Jio’s digital distribution capabilities with Allianz’s global insurance expertise. In September 2026 , the HSBC Global Entrepreneurial Wealth Report 2026 found that 74% of Indian entrepreneurs surveyed were considering either relocating abroad or obtaining an additional overseas residency, compared with a global average of about 70%. Singapore was the most preferred destination among Indian respondents. The report also highlighted strong adoption of artificial intelligence among Indian business owners , with entrepreneurs increasingly investing in AI to improve productivity, business models and competitiveness. Economy: On 30 September 2026 , the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved higher Minimum Support Prices for all six mandated Rabi crops for the 2027-28 marketing season . Wheat MSP was fixed at ₹2,610 per quintal , barley at ₹2,286, gram at ₹5,958, lentil at ₹7,390, rapeseed and mustard at ₹6,613 and safflower at ₹7,215. Safflower received the highest absolute increase of ₹675 per quintal , followed by rapeseed and mustard with an increase of ₹413. On 30 September 2026 , the Agriculture Ministry separately approved ₹5,547.99 crore of MSP procurement under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for pulses and oilseeds in Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana for the Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27. Around 7.06 lakh metric tonnes of commodities are planned for procurement. Uttar Pradesh received the largest approved procurement value of approximately ₹3,992.57 crore , followed by Karnataka and Telangana. The decision aims to protect farmers when market prices fall below MSP. On 30 September 2026 , the Cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III (GEC-III) with an estimated outlay of ₹1.86 lakh crore . The programme will strengthen intra-state transmission infrastructure to enable evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable-energy capacity and provide 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems . The project is targeted for implementation by FY 2032-33. It is intended to improve grid stability, reduce renewable-energy curtailment and enable greater integration of solar and wind power into India’s electricity network. From 1 October 2026 , the Government of India reduced export duties on diesel and Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) . The export levy on diesel was reduced from ₹20 to ₹16 per litre , while the levy on ATF was cut from ₹15 to ₹10.50 per litre . The duty on petrol remained unchanged at ₹0.50 per litre . The move forms part of the government’s periodic review of petroleum-product export taxation based on global market conditions and domestic fuel availability. Defence: In late September 2026 , Indian drone company Zuppa Geo Navigation Technologies and the Tamil Nadu Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Corporation (TNUAVC) agreed to develop a specialised drone-pilot and maintenance training programme for Indian Army personnel. The programme aims to train more than 2,000 Army personnel and Agniveers over three years , beginning in October 2026. Training will include classroom instruction, simulation and practical drone flying and is expected to prepare participants for DGCA-authorised Remote Pilot Certification for eligible drone categories. Military Exercise: The second edition of the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise (AIME-2026) commenced on 28 September 2026 at Subic Bay in the Philippines . Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish participated along with maritime forces from ASEAN member states. The exercise was conducted under the theme “Anchored in Trust, United at Sea.” It included harbour interactions, professional exchanges and a sea phase designed to improve interoperability, maritime cooperation and mutual understanding between India and ASEAN navies. MoUs: On 28 September 2026 , the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) signed an MoU in New Delhi for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s tribal cultural heritage . The partnership aims to systematically record traditional knowledge, languages, customs, art forms and cultural practices of tribal communities. IGNCA, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, will provide research and documentation expertise to support long-term preservation and dissemination of tribal traditions. Sports: On 1 October 2026 , the International Cricket Council (ICC) released the schedule for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027 , which will be hosted jointly by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia . The tournament will begin on 2 October 2027 and conclude with the final in Johannesburg on 21 November . Fourteen teams will participate. India will begin its campaign against Australia in Cape Town on 7 October , while the India-Pakistan match is scheduled for 10 October in Johannesburg . On 2 October 2026 , the Indian women’s recurve archery team of Kumkum Mohod, Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma won India’s first-ever Asian Games gold medal in the women’s recurve team event . India defeated powerhouse South Korea 5-3 in set points in the final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan. South Korea had historically dominated this discipline, making India’s victory particularly significant. The medal represented a major breakthrough for Indian recurve archery at the continental level. On 2 October 2026 , Indian boxer Lovlina Borgohain won the women’s 75 kg boxing gold medal at the Asian Games on her 29th birthday . She defeated China’s Ziyi Bao by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It was Lovlina’s first Asian Games gold and made her only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing title. The victory also ended India’s 12-year wait for a women’s boxing gold at the Games. On 2 October 2026 , Indian boxer Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65 kg category at the Asian Games. She defeated Chinese Taipei’s Nien-chin Chen 3-2 in a closely contested final. The victory was particularly significant because Chen was an Olympic medallist and one of Asia’s established boxers. Parveen’s gold formed part of a strong Indian boxing performance on Day 14 of the Games and reinforced India’s growing strength across multiple women’s boxing categories. On 2 October 2026 , Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal won the men’s freestyle 65 kg gold medal at the Asian Games after producing a remarkable comeback against Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev . Sujeet trailed 2-9 during the final but scored decisive takedowns in the closing stages to win 10-9 . His victory added him to the list of Indian wrestlers who have won Asian Games gold in the 65 kg category and was one of India’s most dramatic victories of the Games. On 2 October 2026 , the Indian women’s hockey team defeated defending champion China 1-0 in the Asian Games final to win its first gold medal in 44 years . Lalremsiami scored the decisive goal in the 10th minute, while goalkeeper Savita Punia made crucial saves, including a penalty stroke. India’s previous women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games came in 1982 . The victory also secured India a direct qualification berth for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games . On 2 October 2026 , India enjoyed a major medal surge on Day 14 of the Asian Games , winning multiple gold medals across archery, boxing, wrestling and hockey . Gold-medal winners included the women’s recurve archery team, boxers Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda, wrestler Sujeet Kalkal and the women’s hockey team. The day became one of India’s strongest single-day performances at the Games and significantly improved its position in the overall medal standings. In the final, she recovered from an early deficit and forced a shoot-off before hitting a perfect 10 to secure victory. Kumkum had already been part of India’s gold-winning women’s recurve team, making it her second gold of the Games. Her achievement ended decades of dominance by traditional archery powerhouses in the individual recurve event. On 3 October 2026 , Indian golfer Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold medal . She finished with a score of 5-under 265 , ending India’s 24-year wait for an individual Asian Games golf title after Shiv Kapur’s victory in 2002. Pranavi also contributed to India’s silver medal in the women’s team competition alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar . Her victory marked one of India’s most important achievements in women’s golf. He will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan . Bagchi has extensive experience across banking, digital financial services and insurance. title: Antler, Nikhil Kamath invest Rs 4 crore in Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis
excerpt: Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Antler and Nikhil Kamath, with participation from investors including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures. The startup plans to use the funding to expand its AI-assisted autism and developmental screening platform across India, as it moves from developing and validating its technology towards wider deployment across public and private healthcare networks. Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis had previously raised its first funding round in 2024 from investors including Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain. “This funding marks a shift for Aignosis from building and validating the technology to taking it into the healthcare system at scale,” said Raksheet Jain, co-founder of Aignosis. “Our focus now is to make autism screening more accessible, strengthen the referral pathway around it, and build a model that can work across both public and private healthcare settings,” he said. How the screening system works Aignosis has developed a screening system intended to help identify children who may require further clinical assessment for autism and other developmental concerns. The system uses a standard laptop and webcam and is designed for children aged between 16 months and nine years. During a short video involving nine stimulus modules, computer vision technology analyses behavioural signals including gaze, response to name and reactions to facial expressions. The system then generates a risk report indicating whether further clinical assessment may be required. It does not provide a diagnosis. Aignosis said it has completed the regulatory process with India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation and received Class B certification for its screening technology. The startup was incubated at IIMA Ventures and was also selected for Google's 2025 Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First programme. Google said Aignosis was among 20 startups selected for the cohort from more than 1,600 applications. The startup was also selected for BFI VK Connect and participated in a three-week immersion programme in Europe. Expanding through clinics and health centres Aignosis primarily operates through what it calls a Clinic-in-Clinic model, under which its screening technology is deployed through paediatricians rather than being sold as a standalone device. The approach is intended to allow paediatricians to incorporate developmental screening into their practices and identify children who may require further assessment or referral. It is currently deployed across more than 20 government primary healthcare centres in Rajasthan. Aignosis said it has also partnered with Mankind Pharma, whose medical representatives are supporting screening camps with paediatricians across India. It is beginning operations with Apollo SHINE Foundation across about 125 schools. “Most healthcare innovation in India is built for the top of the pyramid and never leaves it. Aignosis is going the other way, starting in government health centres and small clinics, not private hospitals in metros. That's distribution thinking that actually moves the needle at scale,” said Nikhil Kamath, an investor in the startup. Targeting 100,000 screenings According to the startup, it has completed more than 8,000 screenings so far and aims to take the total to at least 100,000 by the end of FY2026-27. As part of its expansion, the startup is preparing to enter Punjab, the National Capital Region, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Maharashtra. It plans to use its experience in Rajasthan as a reference for wider government adoption while expanding screening and referral access across public and private healthcare networks. The expansion comes as the startup looks to increase access to early developmental screening through paediatric clinics, government health centres and schools in different parts of India.

title: Telengana Governor Inaugurates FPTA 65th AGM & Conference 2026
excerpt: The three-day FPTA 65 th Annual General Meeting & Conference 2026; hosted by The Federation of Paper Traders’ Association (FPTA), the apex national body representing paper traders; in collaboration with the Telangana Paper Merchants’ Association (TPMA), was inaugurated by H.E. Sri Shiv Pratap Shukla, Hon’ble Governor of Telangana; at the Novotel HICC, Madhapur. Chief Guest Sri Rajesh Ponnuru, CEO, ITC Ltd. (PSPD); Guests of Honour Sri Pawan Agarwal, President, IPMA & CMD, Naini Papers Ltd.; Sri A.S. Mehta, President & Director, JK Paper Ltd.; and Sri Sushil Kumar Khetan, CEO & Whole Time Director, Emami Paper Mills Ltd., graced the occasion. The meeting was presided over by Sri Rajesh Jain, President, FPTA and joined by Sri T. Kishan Singh, President Nominee, FPTA; Sri Abhishek Vijaywargiya, President, TPMA; Sri Prasad RG, Chairman, Reception Committee, FPTA 65 th AGM; and Sri Ashish Jain Bhansali, Hon. Secretary, TPMA. More than 1,000 paper traders from across India are attending the Conference, being held from October 3 rd to 5 th , 2026. The event returns to Hyderabad after 19 years and has added significance for the city as Sri T. Kishan Singh, Managing Director, Tirumala Balaji Paper Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad, is set to take over as Nominee President of FPTA. H.E. Sri Shiv Pratap Shukla, Hon’ble Governor of Telangana; addressing the gathering said, The paper industry does not deplete natural forests, as raw timber is ethically sourced from fast-growing agroforestry crops like poplar, cultivated specifically by farmers for quick harvest cycles. Popular slogans like "Save Paper, Save Trees" misinform the public; therefore, industry leadership must actively educate society that paper production supports rural farming economies rather than destroying natural forest habitats. While broadcast and digital channels produce fleeting news that is quickly forgotten or recycled, physical newsprint remains the trusted, authentic medium for daily reflection, focused reading, and public dialogue. Although digitization may lead to a "less paper" world, a completely "paperless" society is impossible because history, culture, official governance, and formal representations will always be anchored on physical paper. To address tax discrepancies, such as an 18% GST on paper alongside 0% on notebooks, the industry must pursue constructive representation over hostile agitation. As a ₹1-lakh-crore tax-paying sector, trade bodies should present clear, structured memorandums to state representatives, the Finance Minister, and the GST Council to achieve tax equity across states through persistent, strategic engagement. Beyond commercial interests, public campaigns should advocate for responsible usage, teaching younger generations to respect and preserve paper rather than waste it. Paper remains the fundamental driver of literacy, publishing, and cultural continuity, guiding learners from childhood slates to complex educational and intellectual pursuits. Ultimately, paper safeguards India's rich intellectual tradition, carrying forward a legacy of global knowledge leadership that traces back to ancient learning centers like Taxila and Nalanda. As India advances toward becoming a developed nation and global leader by 2047, the paper industry serves as an essential engine for commerce, education, and national pride. Reflecting on an impactful tenure, the outgoing FPTA President Sri Rajesh Jain, highlighted nation-wide engagement after visiting 35 of 36 affiliated associations. He said, the key initiatives included eight educational webinars, the FPTA Champions Cricket Trophy, an international study tour to China, the inaugural Regional South Meet in Kodaikanal, and celebrating Paper Day at Bharat Mandapam alongside industry leaders and government dignitaries. To strengthen the paper ecosystem, FPTA built strong collaborative ties with mill organizations like IPMA and IRMA while partnering with major trade bodies including ASSOCHAM, FICCI, and CAIT. Demonstrating active policy advocacy, the leadership submitted formal representations to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Nitin Gadkari to resolve the inverted GST duty structure affecting notebook manufacturers. Concluding with gratitude to the FPTA team, host associations, family, and TPMA for organizing the 65th AGM, leadership was warmly handed over to incoming President Mr. Kishan to drive future progress. Sri Sushil Kumar Khetan, Ceo & Whole Time Director, Emami Paper Mills Ltd.; said, The Indian paper industry has a promising future, with rising consumption and significant headroom in per-capita usage. Paper remains essential across education, publishing, printing, pharmaceuticals and packaging. The dealer and distributor is not merely a link between mills and customers but the eyes and ears of the industry, with a growing role as a market developer. Packaging, particularly for FMCG, food, pharmaceuticals, retail and e-commerce, will be a major growth engine, while specialty and value-added papers offer further opportunities. Customers increasingly demand quality, consistency and service, not merely competitive pricing. The industry must embrace sustainability, recycling, automation, digitalisation, AI and process innovation to become globally competitive. Mills and dealers need to move from transactional relationships to strategic partnerships, jointly understanding customer needs and creating new demand. The future lies not merely in selling more paper, but in creating more reasons for India to use paper, while building an innovative, sustainable and globally competitive industry. Sri A.S. Mehta, President & Director, Jk Paper Ltd.; said, the paper ecosystem is around four "minars", like the minars in Charminar: manufacturing, distribution, selling, and customers. While geopolitical volatility and raw material constraints cause prolonged market impacts, the core lesson is building self-reliance, Atmanirbhar. To stay competitive, paper distribution and sales must evolve alongside manufacturing by adopting digital tools, AI, and deep customer insights. Additionally, the industry must prioritize sustainability through raw material security and resource-efficient technology . Despite global uncertainties, India’s rising income levels present massive long-term market potential for paper and packaging applications. Rather than dwelling on negative headlines, paper trade stakeholders must rethink traditional models and discover "another way" of selling to create and realize sustainable value across the entire ecosystem. Chief Guest Sri Rajesh Ponnuru, Ceo, Itc Ltd. (Pspd); The Indian paper industry is a vital pillar of national progress and employment, supported by over 5 lakh farmers, 600 mills, 6,000 traders, and 1 lakh printers. Reimagining its raw material model, the sector is deeply inclusive and sustainable sourcing 75% of fiber from recycled materials, 8% from agro-residues, and 20% from tree-based farming, while matching top global resource-efficiency standards. Paper traders play a crucial role in managing complex supply chains , supporting MSMEs, and facilitating the shift from single-use plastics to eco-friendly packaging. However, to maintain global competitiveness and safeguard domestic investments, structural challenges must be addressed. Key among these is rectifying the inverted duty structure under GST and implementing protective trade measures against unfair foreign competition. As India progresses economically, sustained growth relies on nurturing this farmer-partner model through continuous innovation, trade policy alignment, and collaborative industry leadership. Sri Abhishek Vijaywargiya, President, Telangana Paper Merchants’ Association, said, When historians write the story of civilisation, they speak of great nations, leaders and inventions. Yet, behind them all was paper, the medium that preserved ideas, recorded discoveries and carried knowledge across generations. Before a scientist made a breakthrough, a doctor earned a degree, an entrepreneur built an enterprise or a leader governed a nation, each first learned from a book and recorded thoughts on paper. A notebook may cost only a few rupees, but the future written in it is priceless. We are not merely trading a product; we are moving knowledge, opportunity and aspiration. In the age of AI and digital transformation, the future is not paper versus digital, it is paper and digital together. Growth and sustainability must move hand in hand. Sri Ashish Jain Bhansali, Hon. Secretary, TPMA, said, The Telangana Paper Merchants' Association (TPMA) anchors its identity in community service, member empowerment, and active industry advocacy. Demonstrating social commitment, TPMA annually distributes 12,000 notebooks, supports Ekal Vidyalaya, has adopted over seven schools for 25 years, and funds healthcare and educational infrastructure. To navigate evolving market dynamics, TPMA offers regular seminars on GST and regulations, organizes annual mill visits, and operates an arbitration committee to resolve commercial disputes. The association also actively champions trade concerns before government authorities on critical policy and tax issues. Combining heritage with technological innovation, TPMA’s vision centers on unity, youth empowerment, and collaborative growth. With this spirit, TPMA warmly welcomes the entire paper trade fraternity to the 65 th FPTA AGM & Conference 2026 in Hyderabad to collectively write the next chapter of the Indian paper industry. Sri T. Kishan Singh, President Nominee, FPTA, said, paper traders serve as the vital link between paper mills and consumers, supplying publishers, notebook manufacturers, printers, converters and several other industries. Paper is not just another commodity; it is part of our lives, our economy and nation-building. Our message is simple, Support paper, Use paper, Love paper. He urged the Government to recognise the sector’s needs, particularly the shortage of suitable warehouse space. Finding affordable locations to store paper and efficiently supply it to industries is a major challenge, including in Hyderabad. Paper Industry's Prospects India is the world’s third-largest paper-producing country, with annual production capacity of around 25 million tonnes, growing at approximately 5.8–6% annually. The paper and paperboard trade volume is estimated at 23.84 million tonnes, while the paper and related-products trading sector has an indicative turnover of around ₹50,000 crore, growing by about 7–10% annually. The combined Andhra Pradesh and Telangana market is estimated at around ₹3,600 crore, including approximately ₹1,650 crore in Telangana and ₹1,000 crore in Hyderabad. The industry sees considerable scope to increase consumption through education, publishing, printing, packaging, e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, FMCG and manufacturing, besides promoting sustainable paper-based alternatives to single-use plastics. FPTA also seeks to dispel the misconception that paper consumption necessarily causes deforestation. Industry data indicates that 74–76% of Indian paper production is based on recovered/recycled fibre, while 18–20% is wood-based and 6–8% comes from agricultural residue, such as bagasse. The industry advocates responsible consumption, recycling and sustainable sourcing to strengthen paper as a renewable and recyclable material.

title: Telangana steps up child online safety with new framework
excerpt: HYDERABAD: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday directed officials to prepare a comprehensive Child Online Safety Framework to protect children from cybercrimes and ensure access to justice. The state will prepare the framework in consultation with the Telangana High Court and the Telangana State Legal Services Authority (TGSLSA). Reddy made the announcement while […] HYDERABAD: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday directed officials to prepare a comprehensive Child Online Safety Framework to protect children from cybercrimes and ensure access to justice. The state will prepare the framework in consultation with the Telangana High Court and the Telangana State Legal Services Authority (TGSLSA). Reddy made the announcement while addressing the inaugural session of the National Legal Services Authority’s South Zone Regional Conference in Hyderabad. Parents to be involved in child safety framework The conference focused on the theme “Justice for Children in Cyberspace.” Union Minister of State for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal, Telangana High Court Chief Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Supreme Court judges Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Alok Aradhe, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice P S Narasimha, and Telangana High Court judge Justice P Sam Koshy attended the event. Reddy called for parents to take part in framing the Child Online Safety Framework. He also urged families to stay alert to online risks faced by children. “Every child and parent should know two numbers: 1930 for cybercrime and 1098 for child help,” he said. The Chief Minister asked parents to speak openly with their children and remain aware of their online activities. “Be curious, not judgemental,” he said. “Protecting children and women remains the highest priority of our government,” Reddy said. Telangana has several institutions working with the police to protect children. These include Bharosa centres, Child Protection Units, Child Welfare Committees, Special Courts and Legal Services Authorities. CM launches bonded labour legal aid scheme Reddy said Bharosa centres offer police support, medical assistance, legal aid and counselling to women and children under one roof. Hyderabad also has India’s first Child Friendly Court, he said. The police department’s Women Safety Wing runs SHE-Bharosa Cyber Labs to help protect children online. Reddy also highlighted the CybHER app, which helps students and teachers learn about online safety. The state also trains students as cyber ambassadors to help their classmates stay safe online. TGSLSA has signed a memorandum of understanding with the School Education department. Through this initiative, teachers educate children about their legal rights. More than 3,000 Child Protection Officers have also received training, Reddy said. The Chief Minister launched the TGSLSA Freedom from Bonded Labour – Legal Aid, Rescue, Rehabilitation and Re-integration Scheme, 2026 . The scheme provides a mechanism to report bonded labour cases and aims to create greater awareness about labour rights. Reddy reiterated the government’s commitment to strengthening Legal Services Authorities and expanding their reach to every district and village. Justice must restore dignity, says CM “Justice is not only about conviction. It is about restoration. It is about dignity. It is about giving back children their childhood,” Reddy said. Referring to Mahatma Gandhi’s fight for the weak and poor through the law, the Chief Minister highlighted the role of Legal Services Authorities in ensuring access to justice. Reddy said the internet and artificial intelligence have brought several positive changes to society. However, he warned that children can also face risks from misinformation and online crimes. “Children can make mistakes and its consequences can be bad for themselves, for their families, and for the society. Internet did not create these crimes, but it has made it easier to organise them on a global scale,” he said. The Chief Minister said the key challenge was to prevent cybercrimes against children, keep them safe online and ensure that they receive justice. Reddy welcomed the decision to host the conference in Hyderabad and expressed confidence that its recommendations would guide Telangana and other states across the country. ]]>

title: Orange Retail Finance raises Rs 100 crore in debt, adds Rs 100 crore Shriram co-lending partnership to fuel expansion
excerpt: 13 years ago, Orange Retail Finance was a Chennai lender writing loans for two-wheelers sold through dealerships. Last month, it raised Rs 100 crore in debt from investors and added a Rs 100 crore co-lending partnership with Shriram, both aimed at funding a very different loan book. The Rs 100 crore came through listed non-convertible debentures (NCD) arranged with UMI Capital. It is half of a Rs 200 crore NCD programme the company set up for this financial year, and part of a wider Rs 300 crore debt target it plans to meet through further issuances and borrowing from banks and other institutions. Notably, Orange is also planning to raise Rs 100 crore of equity capital. The partnership with Shriram The co-lending partnership with Shriram gives Orange Rs 100 crore to lend without putting the full amount on its own balance sheet. In a co-lending arrangement , the larger partner takes most of each loan onto its books while the smaller NBFC originates the loan, keeps the customer relationship and holds a minority share. For a lender of Orange's size, it is the difference between growing at the pace its own capital allows and growing at the pace its branches can actually find customers. This is not new territory for the company. Co-lending already funds about a quarter of what Orange has out on loan, with three NBFC partners accounting for roughly Rs 101 crore of its book as of June, according to ICRA. Adding Shriram, one of India's largest retail NBFCs, extends that model considerably. Expanding beyond two-wheeler loans Orange had Rs 401 crore in assets under management as of 30 June 2026 and is targeting Rs 550 crore by the end of this financial year, which means growing roughly 37% in the remaining months. The growth is meant to come from gold loans and MSME loans against property rather than two-wheelers, with home loans and other secured products alongside them. And that shift is already visible: loans against property made up 58% of the book in June, overtaking two-wheelers at 41%. Six months earlier, the ratio was the other way round. Gold loans are the newer bet and are starting from a much smaller base. The company has said every one of its branches will have gold loan infrastructure in place by October 2026, which is what turns a product it currently does very little of into something that can carry a share of the year's target. Orange currently runs 58 branches across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, and plans to reach 150 branches and about 1,500 employees, with a longer-term ambition of Rs 3,000 crore in AUM by FY31. The company has been through a few cycles while getting here. It has traded through demonetisation in 2016 and the COVID-19 years, and said each of those forced it to rebuild rather than hold on to what it had, including its credit and risk frameworks and its move away from a dealer-led model. Onboarding CXO team To support this expansion, Orange has onboarded a CXO team across finance, business and operations, risk, technology and treasury to tighten governance, risk management and financial discipline as it scales. “We want to combine the strength of our people and customer relationships with the intelligence of technology and the discipline of institutional finance. That is how we believe we can build a financial institution that lasts,” said Ebenezer Daniel G, Founder and CEO of Orange Retail Finance. On technology, Orange is investing in AI, automation and digital credit processes , but frames it as support for staff who already know the local market rather than a replacement for them. Ebenezer Daniel said the company's 13 years had taught it that the strongest organisations are not those that simply survive difficult times but those with the courage to transform because of them. “Our ambition is not merely to become larger, but to become a trusted neighbourhood financial institution, one that stays close to customers, understands communities and creates meaningful value in their lives,” Ebenezer Daniel added.

title: Current Affairs One-Liner: 3rd October 2026
excerpt: National: On 30 September 2026 , the Union Cabinet approved an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) for Delhi with an estimated cost of ₹1,789.52 crore . The project will cover 42 major traffic corridors and use technologies such as AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, automatic enforcement and real-time traffic monitoring. It is intended to reduce congestion, improve emergency-vehicle movement and strengthen traffic management. The same Cabinet meeting also approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III , making both decisions important infrastructure-related developments. On 30 September 2026 , Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched implementation guidelines for National Coastal Mission 2.0 (NCM 2.0) in New Delhi. The ₹767-crore Central Sector Scheme will operate until 2030-31 across nine coastal states and four Union Territories . It focuses on coastal ecosystem restoration, pollution management, vulnerability assessment, sustainable tourism, biodiversity conservation and climate resilience. The programme also seeks to unlock opportunities under India’s Blue Economy while protecting coastal communities and natural ecosystems. On 2 October 2026 , the Tamil Nadu government expanded the Vettri Payanam free bus travel scheme for women and transgender persons. A total of 12,692 government buses were brought under the expanded programme, including several express, deluxe and mofussil services. The scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day . By reducing travel costs, the initiative aims to improve access to employment, education, healthcare and public services while promoting greater mobility and economic participation among women. On 2 October 2026 , the Government of India, in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh, formally identified 28 places and geographical features using standard names on the official Survey of India map . These include peaks, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes and land areas. The move is intended to improve accurate geographical identification and public awareness. Some of the locations are in strategically sensitive areas of Ladakh, making the development important from both administrative and national-security perspectives. On 2 October 2026 , Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal under the Mumbai Port Authority was declared India’s first plastic-free oil terminal . The announcement was made during Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 led by Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal . The initiative focuses on eliminating single-use plastic and making port operations more environmentally sustainable. Jawahar Dweep is an important petroleum-handling facility of Mumbai Port, and its plastic-free status supports broader cleanliness and sustainability efforts in India’s maritime sector. On 2 October 2026 , the foundation stone was laid for the Global Horticulture Hub – Rayalaseema Rising at Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh . The project envisages investment of around ₹1 lakh crore and is planned in three phases across 10 districts. It will cover 201 clusters, more than 300 mandals and thousands of villages. The project aims to strengthen horticulture production, food processing, exports, logistics and farmer incomes while positioning Rayalaseema as a major global horticulture and agri-business centre. In October 2026 , President Droupadi Murmu gave assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 , clearing the final constitutional step required before implementation by the state. The law seeks to establish a common framework for selected civil matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and related personal-law issues. Gujarat had already passed the Bill earlier in 2026, so the fresh development is specifically the President’s assent , rather than introduction of the legislation itself. Banking: On 30 September 2026 , the Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved the proposed acquisition of certain equity shares in IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company Limited by BNP Paribas Cardif . BNP Paribas Cardif is a wholly owned subsidiary of France-based BNP Paribas, while IndiaFirst Life is an IRDAI-licensed life insurer operating in India. The CCI examines mergers and acquisitions to ensure that proposed combinations do not adversely affect competition. On 30 September 2026 , Jio Financial Services Ltd and Allianz Europe B.V. jointly invested ₹640.10 crore in their 50:50 joint venture, Jio Allianz General Insurance Ltd , through a rights issue. Each partner contributed ₹320.05 crore . The funds are intended to support the insurer’s business operations and expansion. Jio Financial and Allianz had earlier entered into a 50:50 partnership covering general and health insurance, combining Jio’s digital distribution capabilities with Allianz’s global insurance expertise. In September 2026 , the HSBC Global Entrepreneurial Wealth Report 2026 found that 74% of Indian entrepreneurs surveyed were considering either relocating abroad or obtaining an additional overseas residency, compared with a global average of about 70%. Singapore was the most preferred destination among Indian respondents. The report also highlighted strong adoption of artificial intelligence among Indian business owners , with entrepreneurs increasingly investing in AI to improve productivity, business models and competitiveness. Economy: On 30 September 2026 , the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved higher Minimum Support Prices for all six mandated Rabi crops for the 2027-28 marketing season . Wheat MSP was fixed at ₹2,610 per quintal , barley at ₹2,286, gram at ₹5,958, lentil at ₹7,390, rapeseed and mustard at ₹6,613 and safflower at ₹7,215. Safflower received the highest absolute increase of ₹675 per quintal , followed by rapeseed and mustard with an increase of ₹413. On 30 September 2026 , the Agriculture Ministry separately approved ₹5,547.99 crore of MSP procurement under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for pulses and oilseeds in Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana for the Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27. Around 7.06 lakh metric tonnes of commodities are planned for procurement. Uttar Pradesh received the largest approved procurement value of approximately ₹3,992.57 crore , followed by Karnataka and Telangana. The decision aims to protect farmers when market prices fall below MSP. On 30 September 2026 , the Cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III (GEC-III) with an estimated outlay of ₹1.86 lakh crore . The programme will strengthen intra-state transmission infrastructure to enable evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable-energy capacity and provide 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems . The project is targeted for implementation by FY 2032-33. It is intended to improve grid stability, reduce renewable-energy curtailment and enable greater integration of solar and wind power into India’s electricity network. From 1 October 2026 , the Government of India reduced export duties on diesel and Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) . The export levy on diesel was reduced from ₹20 to ₹16 per litre , while the levy on ATF was cut from ₹15 to ₹10.50 per litre . The duty on petrol remained unchanged at ₹0.50 per litre . The move forms part of the government’s periodic review of petroleum-product export taxation based on global market conditions and domestic fuel availability. Defence: In late September 2026 , Indian drone company Zuppa Geo Navigation Technologies and the Tamil Nadu Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Corporation (TNUAVC) agreed to develop a specialised drone-pilot and maintenance training programme for Indian Army personnel. The programme aims to train more than 2,000 Army personnel and Agniveers over three years , beginning in October 2026. Training will include classroom instruction, simulation and practical drone flying and is expected to prepare participants for DGCA-authorised Remote Pilot Certification for eligible drone categories. Military Exercise: The second edition of the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise (AIME-2026) commenced on 28 September 2026 at Subic Bay in the Philippines . Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish participated along with maritime forces from ASEAN member states. The exercise was conducted under the theme “Anchored in Trust, United at Sea.” It included harbour interactions, professional exchanges and a sea phase designed to improve interoperability, maritime cooperation and mutual understanding between India and ASEAN navies. MoUs: On 28 September 2026 , the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) signed an MoU in New Delhi for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s tribal cultural heritage . The partnership aims to systematically record traditional knowledge, languages, customs, art forms and cultural practices of tribal communities. IGNCA, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, will provide research and documentation expertise to support long-term preservation and dissemination of tribal traditions. Sports: On 1 October 2026 , the International Cricket Council (ICC) released the schedule for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027 , which will be hosted jointly by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia . The tournament will begin on 2 October 2027 and conclude with the final in Johannesburg on 21 November . Fourteen teams will participate. India will begin its campaign against Australia in Cape Town on 7 October , while the India-Pakistan match is scheduled for 10 October in Johannesburg . On 2 October 2026 , the Indian women’s recurve archery team of Kumkum Mohod, Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma won India’s first-ever Asian Games gold medal in the women’s recurve team event . India defeated powerhouse South Korea 5-3 in set points in the final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan. South Korea had historically dominated this discipline, making India’s victory particularly significant. The medal represented a major breakthrough for Indian recurve archery at the continental level. On 2 October 2026 , Indian boxer Lovlina Borgohain won the women’s 75 kg boxing gold medal at the Asian Games on her 29th birthday . She defeated China’s Ziyi Bao by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It was Lovlina’s first Asian Games gold and made her only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing title. The victory also ended India’s 12-year wait for a women’s boxing gold at the Games. On 2 October 2026 , Indian boxer Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65 kg category at the Asian Games. She defeated Chinese Taipei’s Nien-chin Chen 3-2 in a closely contested final. The victory was particularly significant because Chen was an Olympic medallist and one of Asia’s established boxers. Parveen’s gold formed part of a strong Indian boxing performance on Day 14 of the Games and reinforced India’s growing strength across multiple women’s boxing categories. On 2 October 2026 , Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal won the men’s freestyle 65 kg gold medal at the Asian Games after producing a remarkable comeback against Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev . Sujeet trailed 2-9 during the final but scored decisive takedowns in the closing stages to win 10-9 . His victory added him to the list of Indian wrestlers who have won Asian Games gold in the 65 kg category and was one of India’s most dramatic victories of the Games. On 2 October 2026 , the Indian women’s hockey team defeated defending champion China 1-0 in the Asian Games final to win its first gold medal in 44 years . Lalremsiami scored the decisive goal in the 10th minute, while goalkeeper Savita Punia made crucial saves, including a penalty stroke. India’s previous women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games came in 1982 . The victory also secured India a direct qualification berth for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games . On 2 October 2026 , India enjoyed a major medal surge on Day 14 of the Asian Games , winning multiple gold medals across archery, boxing, wrestling and hockey . Gold-medal winners included the women’s recurve archery team, boxers Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda, wrestler Sujeet Kalkal and the women’s hockey team. The day became one of India’s strongest single-day performances at the Games and significantly improved its position in the overall medal standings. On 3 October 2026 , 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod created history by becoming the first Indian recurve archer to win an individual Asian Games gold medal . In the final, she recovered from an early deficit and forced a shoot-off before hitting a perfect 10 to secure victory. Kumkum had already been part of India’s gold-winning women’s recurve team, making it her second gold of the Games. Her achievement ended decades of dominance by traditional archery powerhouses in the individual recurve event. On 3 October 2026 , Indian golfer Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold medal . She finished with a score of 5-under 265 , ending India’s 24-year wait for an individual Asian Games golf title after Shiv Kapur’s victory in 2002. Pranavi also contributed to India’s silver medal in the women’s team competition alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar . Her victory marked one of India’s most important achievements in women’s golf. Appointments: In October 2026 , the Reserve Bank of India approved the appointment of Anup Bagchi as Managing Director and CEO of HDFC Bank for a three-year term beginning 27 October 2026 . He will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan . Bagchi has extensive experience across banking, digital financial services and insurance. Since HDFC Bank is India’s largest private-sector lender, leadership changes at the bank are particularly important for banking and financial-awareness examinations. Important Days: World Rivers Day was observed on 27 September 2026 , as it is traditionally marked on the fourth Sunday of September . The observance promotes awareness about the importance of rivers, freshwater ecosystems and sustainable water management. It encourages communities, governments and environmental organisations to protect rivers from pollution, over-extraction, habitat loss and other environmental pressures. The day also highlights the importance of healthy river systems for drinking water, agriculture, biodiversity, livelihoods and climate resilience. Questions: Q1. What was the Minimum Support Price fixed for wheat for the Rabi Marketing Season 2027-28? a) ₹2,500 per quintal b) ₹2,585 per quintal c) ₹2,610 per quintal d) ₹2,675 per quintal Answer: c) ₹2,610 per quintal. The CCEA approved higher MSPs for all six mandated Rabi crops for the 2027-28 marketing season. Wheat MSP was increased by ₹25 from ₹2,585 to ₹2,610 per quintal, while safflower received the highest absolute MSP increase of ₹675 per quintal. Q2. Who has been approved by the RBI as the next Managing Director and CEO of HDFC Bank from 27 October 2026? a) Anup Kumar Saha b) Anup Bagchi c) Sandeep Bakhshi d) Ashok Vaswani Answer: b) Anup Bagchi. RBI approved Anup Bagchi as HDFC Bank’s MD and CEO for a three-year term beginning 27 October 2026. He will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan. Do not confuse him with Anup Kumar Saha, who was appointed to lead Kotak Mahindra Bank.

title: Regulatory frameworks need to evolve with rapidly changing environment: NITI Aayog's Rajiv Gauba
excerpt: The challenge before policymakers is not to choose between regulation and growth, but to develop regulations that manage risks while supporting innovation, competition and investment, Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, said on Saturday.In his address at the plenary session on "Regulatory Oversight in an Age of Disruption" at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave here, he highlighted the need for regulatory frameworks to evolve alongside a rapidly changing geopolitical, technological and economic environment.Gauba observed that geopolitical uncertainty, disruptions to trade routes and global supply chains, and the increasing use of tariffs, export controls and investment restrictions as strategic instruments are reshaping the economic landscape.At the same time, he noted that technological change is advancing faster than many institutions and regulatory frameworks can adapt, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technologies.He also highlighted the growing complexity of modern business models, which increasingly span multiple sectors and technologies.As traditional boundaries between industries become less relevant, he stressed that regulatory frameworks must evolve to address interconnected risks without creating fragmented or conflicting obligations.Gauba also underlined that while regulation is essential for safety, consumer protection, market integrity and systemic stability, excessive or poorly designed regulation can impede innovation, competition and investment.He stressed that national competitiveness depends not only on infrastructure, labour laws and incentives, but also on the clarity, consistency and predictability of the regulatory environment. For businesses considering new investments, he said, the ability to operate at scale and innovate with certainty is an increasingly important consideration.He further emphasised that regulatory independence must go hand in hand with accountability. While regulators need autonomy to take difficult decisions free from undue influence, public confidence requires transparent decision-making, clear procedures, effective review mechanisms and accountability for regulatory performance.He called for greater coordination among regulators to address overlapping mandates, avoid duplication and close regulatory gaps as businesses increasingly operate across traditional regulatory domains.—IANSna/

title: Current Affairs One-Liner: 3rd October 2026
excerpt: National: On 30 September 2026 , the Union Cabinet approved an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) for Delhi with an estimated cost of ₹1,789.52 crore . The project will cover 42 major traffic corridors and use technologies such as AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, automatic enforcement and real-time traffic monitoring. It is intended to reduce congestion, improve emergency-vehicle movement and strengthen traffic management. The same Cabinet meeting also approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III , making both decisions important infrastructure-related developments. On 30 September 2026 , Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched implementation guidelines for National Coastal Mission 2.0 (NCM 2.0) in New Delhi. The ₹767-crore Central Sector Scheme will operate until 2030-31 across nine coastal states and four Union Territories . It focuses on coastal ecosystem restoration, pollution management, vulnerability assessment, sustainable tourism, biodiversity conservation and climate resilience. The programme also seeks to unlock opportunities under India’s Blue Economy while protecting coastal communities and natural ecosystems. On 2 October 2026 , the Tamil Nadu government expanded the Vettri Payanam free bus travel scheme for women and transgender persons. A total of 12,692 government buses were brought under the expanded programme, including several express, deluxe and mofussil services. The scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day . By reducing travel costs, the initiative aims to improve access to employment, education, healthcare and public services while promoting greater mobility and economic participation among women. On 2 October 2026 , the Government of India, in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh, formally identified 28 places and geographical features using standard names on the official Survey of India map . These include peaks, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes and land areas. The move is intended to improve accurate geographical identification and public awareness. Some of the locations are in strategically sensitive areas of Ladakh, making the development important from both administrative and national-security perspectives. On 2 October 2026 , Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal under the Mumbai Port Authority was declared India’s first plastic-free oil terminal . The announcement was made during Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 led by Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal . The initiative focuses on eliminating single-use plastic and making port operations more environmentally sustainable. Jawahar Dweep is an important petroleum-handling facility of Mumbai Port, and its plastic-free status supports broader cleanliness and sustainability efforts in India’s maritime sector. On 2 October 2026 , the foundation stone was laid for the Global Horticulture Hub – Rayalaseema Rising at Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh . The project envisages investment of around ₹1 lakh crore and is planned in three phases across 10 districts. It will cover 201 clusters, more than 300 mandals and thousands of villages. The project aims to strengthen horticulture production, food processing, exports, logistics and farmer incomes while positioning Rayalaseema as a major global horticulture and agri-business centre. In October 2026 , President Droupadi Murmu gave assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 , clearing the final constitutional step required before implementation by the state. The law seeks to establish a common framework for selected civil matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and related personal-law issues. Gujarat had already passed the Bill earlier in 2026, so the fresh development is specifically the President’s assent , rather than introduction of the legislation itself. Banking: On 30 September 2026 , the Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved the proposed acquisition of certain equity shares in IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company Limited by BNP Paribas Cardif . BNP Paribas Cardif is a wholly owned subsidiary of France-based BNP Paribas, while IndiaFirst Life is an IRDAI-licensed life insurer operating in India. Each partner contributed ₹320.05 crore . The funds are intended to support the insurer’s business operations and expansion. Jio Financial and Allianz had earlier entered into a 50:50 partnership covering general and health insurance, combining Jio’s digital distribution capabilities with Allianz’s global insurance expertise. In September 2026 , the HSBC Global Entrepreneurial Wealth Report 2026 found that 74% of Indian entrepreneurs surveyed were considering either relocating abroad or obtaining an additional overseas residency, compared with a global average of about 70%. Singapore was the most preferred destination among Indian respondents. The report also highlighted strong adoption of artificial intelligence among Indian business owners , with entrepreneurs increasingly investing in AI to improve productivity, business models and competitiveness. Economy: On 30 September 2026 , the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved higher Minimum Support Prices for all six mandated Rabi crops for the 2027-28 marketing season . Wheat MSP was fixed at ₹2,610 per quintal , barley at ₹2,286, gram at ₹5,958, lentil at ₹7,390, rapeseed and mustard at ₹6,613 and safflower at ₹7,215. It is intended to improve grid stability, reduce renewable-energy curtailment and enable greater integration of solar and wind power into India’s electricity network. Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish participated along with maritime forces from ASEAN member states. title: Pochampally Ikat products get QR-code tags
excerpt: HYDERABAD: Pochampally Ikat products will carry QR-code tags that allow buyers to verify where a textile was made, how it was produced and details of the weaver. The government has introduced the digital tagging system for Bhudan Pochampally Ikat products. The initiative is aimed at tackling counterfeit products in the market despite the craft already having […] HYDERABAD: Pochampally Ikat products will carry QR-code tags that allow buyers to verify where a textile was made, how it was produced and details of the weaver. The government has introduced the digital tagging system for Bhudan Pochampally Ikat products. The initiative is aimed at tackling counterfeit products in the market despite the craft already having a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. QR code links buyers to weaver details The QR-code system was formally launched last month. Jupitex AI developed the digital technology, which is currently being implemented on a pilot basis for products made by selected weavers. A unique QR code has been linked to every Pochampally handloom textile covered by the system. When scanned, the code opens a dedicated website carrying a certificate of authentication in Telugu and English. The website also provides the weaver’s photograph, village and mandal details, besides the Geo-Tag number of the loom registered with the Department of Handlooms and Textiles. The system is expected to help buyers verify the authenticity of handloom products and give individual weavers greater visibility. Initiative targets counterfeit Ikat products Pochampally Ikat has demand in India and overseas. The source copy says Pochampally designs are being copied at mills in Surat, Ahmedabad and Rajkot in Gujarat. A silk saree that costs about ₹10,000 when made on a handloom after considerable time and labour is being replicated on powerlooms and printing machines and sold for ₹250 to ₹500, according to the source. The availability of cheaper imitation products has affected sales of genuine handloom textiles and caused losses to Pochampally weavers. Tourism and skills programmes planned The district administration has also entered into an understanding with United Way of Hyderabad to support handloom families and improve their livelihoods. Under the partnership, weavers at the grassroots level will receive training in contemporary designs, skill development and capacity building. Support will also be provided for social development. The district administration is also combining technology, tourism and skills training to promote Pochampally Ikat. The Creative Economy Impact Collective (CEIC) has developed tourism trails that will introduce visitors to the history of Pochampally handloom weaving, local food traditions and the lifestyle of weavers. The trails will allow tourists to visit looms directly and observe the weaving process. Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district collector Anurag Jayanti has taken the initiative to introduce the QR-code system as a measure to address the problem of counterfeit products. In the first phase, the system is being implemented through handloom cooperative societies in Bhudan Pochampally and Gundala. The district administration plans to bring all primary handloom cooperative societies, master weavers, producers, members of tie-and-dye associations and retail cloth showrooms under the system. The system will eventually be expanded so that every saree sold at participating showrooms carries a QR code. ]]>

title: Antler, Nikhil Kamath invest Rs 4 crore in Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis
excerpt: Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Antler and Nikhil Kamath, with participation from investors including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures. The startup plans to use the funding to expand its AI-assisted autism and developmental screening platform across India, as it moves from developing and validating its technology towards wider deployment across public and private healthcare networks. Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis had previously raised its first funding round in 2024 from investors including Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain. “This funding marks a shift for Aignosis from building and validating the technology to taking it into the healthcare system at scale,” said Raksheet Jain, co-founder of Aignosis. “Our focus now is to make autism screening more accessible, strengthen the referral pathway around it, and build a model that can work across both public and private healthcare settings,” he said. How the screening system works Aignosis has developed a screening system intended to help identify children who may require further clinical assessment for autism and other developmental concerns. The system uses a standard laptop and webcam and is designed for children aged between 16 months and nine years. During a short video involving nine stimulus modules, computer vision technology analyses behavioural signals including gaze, response to name and reactions to facial expressions. The system then generates a risk report indicating whether further clinical assessment may be required. It does not provide a diagnosis. Aignosis said it has completed the regulatory process with India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation and received Class B certification for its screening technology. The startup was incubated at IIMA Ventures and was also selected for Google's 2025 Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First programme. Google said Aignosis was among 20 startups selected for the cohort from more than 1,600 applications. The startup was also selected for BFI VK Connect and participated in a three-week immersion programme in Europe. Expanding through clinics and health centres Aignosis primarily operates through what it calls a Clinic-in-Clinic model, under which its screening technology is deployed through paediatricians rather than being sold as a standalone device. The approach is intended to allow paediatricians to incorporate developmental screening into their practices and identify children who may require further assessment or referral. It is currently deployed across more than 20 government primary healthcare centres in Rajasthan. Aignosis said it has also partnered with Mankind Pharma, whose medical representatives are supporting screening camps with paediatricians across India. It is beginning operations with Apollo SHINE Foundation across about 125 schools. “Most healthcare innovation in India is built for the top of the pyramid and never leaves it. Aignosis is going the other way, starting in government health centres and small clinics, not private hospitals in metros. That's distribution thinking that actually moves the needle at scale,” said Nikhil Kamath, an investor in the startup. Targeting 100,000 screenings According to the startup, it has completed more than 8,000 screenings so far and aims to take the total to at least 100,000 by the end of FY2026-27. As part of its expansion, the startup is preparing to enter Punjab, the National Capital Region, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Maharashtra. It plans to use its experience in Rajasthan as a reference for wider government adoption while expanding screening and referral access across public and private healthcare networks. The expansion comes as the startup looks to increase access to early developmental screening through paediatric clinics, government health centres and schools in different parts of India.
